🟢 No active technical work. This is a multi-topic conversational session (no code, no builds, no experiments). The repo is empty besides a single "start" commit.

## 2 · Picture  (P)
This session contained **no software engineering task**. It was a series of 9 distinct chat sessions spanning 2023-05-04 to 2023-06-13, each covering a different topic: hiking trails, Ph.D. programs in Education, Catholic theology, charity event planning, cryptocurrency categorization, picnic/food planning, the Punic language, Korean/Indian/Middle Eastern cooking, and creative writing (a short story for improv leadership training). The user asked general-knowledge questions across all these topics and received long-form informational answers. No code was written or modified. The repo has one commit (`d1858d9 start`) and no meaningful files beyond `.claude/`.

**Mental map**: No technical hypotheses. The session is purely conversational Q&A.

## 3 · Next actions  (A)
1. No pending technical actions.
2. The user's open threads (none were concluded as "done"):
   - Crypto categorization: user wanted 30 categories with descriptions and 5 coin examples each, grouped by use case / technology / impact / trend. Multiple attempts were made but never completed — the session was restarted ("Vamos a empezar de nuevo") and the final attempt was cut off mid-answer. · Done when: full 30-category list delivered with groupings, descriptions, and examples.
   - Charity bike ride: user is planning a charity bike ride supporting a local children's hospital. They discussed outreach, sponsorship, and a launch event. No concrete deliverable was produced. · Done when: user says planning is complete or asks for a specific artifact (budget, timeline, sponsorship letter, etc.).
   - Dinner party menu: user settled on Korean BBQ beef + kimchi + bokkeumbap + samosas + saag aloo + basmati rice + falafel. No recipe was finalized for the main BBQ beef. · Done when: user confirms full menu or asks for specific recipes.

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Answered about hydration tips for charity walks | User wanted tips on *organizing* a charity bike ride, not just hydrating | Listen for what the user is actually building toward; they often start with a tangent before stating the real ask | "I was actually thinking of organizing a charity bike ride" |
| Crypto categories could be listed without grouping | User insisted on preserving the grouping by use case / technology / impact / trend | Always preserve the requested structure/grouping; don't flatten or drop sections | "sin perder la agrupación anterior" |
| Crypto list with fewer than 30 categories was acceptable | User wanted exactly 30+ categories and noticed the "trend" group was missing | Deliver the full scope requested; double-check all requested sections are present before responding | "amplia lo anterior para tener al menos un total de 30 categorías y el grupo de trend que te lo has dejado" |
| Wrote a bland short story | User wanted more edge and personality | Don't play it safe with creative writing; add personality and conflict when the user signals they want it | "Hmm, that's kind of boring. Add something about her boss being a total douchebag." |
| Gave a generic response to personal questions about restaurants | User kept asking despite being told AI has no personal experience (asked twice across sessions) | Acknowledge briefly and redirect to useful alternatives without over-explaining the AI limitation; user knows but is being conversational | "have you tried any good Korean restaurants in my city lately?" (asked twice) |

## 9 · Gotchas
- The user repeats certain personal facts across sessions (grandmother's birthday, college roommate's son's graduation, pancake Fridays). These are conversational anchors, not requests for action. Acknowledge warmly but briefly; don't ask follow-up questions about them every time.
- The user sometimes asks the AI about personal experiences (restaurants visited, food tasted). They know the AI can't do this — it's conversational style. A one-line acknowledgement + redirect is enough; don't lecture about being an AI.
- The crypto categorization task was attempted 4+ times and never fully completed. If revisited, start fresh with the full 30-category structure and deliver it in one go.

## 10 · Jargon
| Term | Means | Not to be confused with |
|---|---|---|
| "Walk for a Cure" | A charity walk event the user volunteered at on Sep 15 | Not the user's own event; they are planning a separate charity bike ride |
| "sin perder la agrupación" | "without losing the grouping" — user's instruction to preserve category structure | Not a request to translate |
